badges.title: Fast Starter
badges.desc: Enrolled in 3 courses in your first month

courses.title: Modern Full-Stack Web Development
courses.description: Master responsive HTML5, modern CSS3 styling, JavaScript ES6+, REST APIs, and full stack application design with practical real-world projects.

syllabus.title: HTML5 Semantic Structure & Modern Web Standards
syllabus.summary: Introduction to semantic markup, accessibility (a11y), clean document tree, and modern HTML best practices.
syllabus.notes: Semantic HTML elements give meaning to your markup. Key tags include <header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <section>, and <footer>. Always use proper alt attributes for images.

syllabus.title: CSS3 Flexbox, Grid & Responsive Layouts
syllabus.summary: Deep dive into CSS Flexbox for 1D layouts and CSS Grid for 2D responsive matrix designs across all screen sizes.
syllabus.notes: Flexbox (display: flex) distributes items along a main axis and cross axis. CSS Grid (display: grid) creates 2D track layouts. Use media queries for responsive breakpoints: 640px, 768px, 1024px.

syllabus.title: JavaScript ES6+: Async/Await, Fetch API & DOM
syllabus.summary: Mastering modern JavaScript asynchronous programming, promises, DOM manipulation, and consuming REST APIs.
syllabus.notes: Promises handle asynchronous state (pending, fulfilled, rejected). Async/Await provides synchronous-looking syntax on top of Promises. Always use try...catch for robust error handling.

syllabus.title: Building Dynamic Single Page Architectures
syllabus.summary: Learn state management, client-side routing, modular components, and persistent storage using LocalStorage.
syllabus.notes: SPAs avoid full page refreshes by updating the DOM dynamically via client-side routing and reactive UI components.

syllabus.title: Backend Integration, RESTful Endpoints & Deployment
syllabus.summary: Connecting frontend with Node.js/Express REST APIs, handling JSON requests, and deploying to cloud production.
syllabus.notes: REST principles include standard HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE. Always sanitize inputs, validate payloads, and configure CORS headers correctly.

courses.title: Python for Data Science & Machine Learning
courses.description: Learn Python from scratch to advanced data analysis, NumPy vectorization, Pandas dataframes, Matplotlib visualization, and core Machine Learning algorithms.

syllabus.title: Python Core Essentials & Data Structures
syllabus.summary: Lists, dictionaries, tuples, sets, list comprehensions, and functional programming constructs in Python.
syllabus.notes: Python lists are mutable, tuples are immutable. Dictionaries offer O(1) average lookup. List comprehensions offer concise syntax: [x**2 for x in nums if x % 2 == 0].

syllabus.title: NumPy Arrays & High Performance Vector Math
syllabus.summary: N-dimensional arrays, broadcasting, vector arithmetic, linear algebra operations, and slicing.
syllabus.notes: NumPy arrays (ndarrays) are stored contiguously in memory, making them up to 50x faster than standard Python lists.

syllabus.title: Pandas DataFrames & Real-world Data Wrangling
syllabus.summary: Data cleaning, missing value imputation, group-by aggregations, merging datasets, and time-series analysis.
syllabus.notes: Use df.dropna() or df.fillna() for null values. Use df.groupby('col').mean() for aggregation. df.describe() gives statistical distribution.

syllabus.title: Exploratory Data Analysis & Visualization
syllabus.summary: Building publication-ready charts using Matplotlib and Seaborn: histograms, heatmaps, and scatter plots.
syllabus.notes: Heatmaps show correlation matrices. Box plots identify outliers and IQR. Pairplots visualize multi-variable relationships.

syllabus.title: Supervised Learning: Regression & Classification
syllabus.summary: Train/test split, Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, and model evaluation metrics (MSE, F1-Score).
syllabus.notes: Always split data into train and test sets to prevent overfitting. Evaluate classification models with Precision, Recall, and AUC-ROC.

courses.title: Advanced Engineering Mathematics & Calculus
courses.description: Comprehensive journey through differential calculus, multivariable integration, vector spaces, and differential equations for STEM students.

syllabus.title: Limits, Continuity & Derivative Rules
syllabus.summary: Formal limit definitions, L'Hopital's rule, product/quotient/chain rules, and tangent rate of change.
syllabus.notes: Derivative represents instantaneous rate of change: f'(x) = lim(h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)]/h. L'Hopital's rule applies when limit yields 0/0 or inf/inf.

syllabus.title: Integration Techniques & Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
syllabus.summary: Integration by parts, trigonometric substitutions, partial fractions, and area under curves.
syllabus.notes: Integration by parts formula: integral(u dv) = u*v - integral(v du). The Fundamental Theorem links differentiation with integration.

syllabus.title: Multivariable Calculus: Gradients & Multiple Integrals
syllabus.summary: Partial derivatives, gradient vector, directional derivatives, and double/triple integrals in polar coordinates.
syllabus.notes: The gradient vector grad(f) points in the direction of greatest rate of increase, and its magnitude is that slope.

syllabus.title: First & Second Order Differential Equations
syllabus.summary: Separation of variables, integrating factors, homogeneous equations, and harmonic oscillators.
syllabus.notes: First order linear ODE: dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x). The integrating factor is I(x) = exp(integral(P(x)dx)).

courses.title: Quantum Physics & Modern Mechanics
courses.description: Explore wave-particle duality, Schrödinger wave equation, quantum entanglement, Planck's constant, and atomic models.

syllabus.title: Wave-Particle Duality & Photoelectric Effect
syllabus.summary: Einstein's photoelectric equation, de Broglie wavelength, and double slit electron interference experiments.
syllabus.notes: Light behaves as both a wave and a stream of discrete photons: E = h * f. De Broglie wavelength: lambda = h / p.

syllabus.title: Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle & Wave Functions
syllabus.summary: Understanding fundamental limits of measurement: Delta(x) * Delta(p) >= h-bar / 2, and probability density.
syllabus.notes: You cannot simultaneously measure exact position and momentum with arbitrary precision. Probability density is given by |Psi|^2.

syllabus.title: The Schrödinger Equation & Particle in a Box
syllabus.summary: Time-dependent and time-independent Schrödinger equations, infinite potential well, and quantized energy states.
syllabus.notes: H * Psi = E * Psi. Energy eigenvalues for a particle in a 1D box of length L: E_n = (n^2 * pi^2 * hbar^2) / (2 * m * L^2).

syllabus.title: Quantum Tunneling & Quantum Computing Foundations
syllabus.summary: Transmission coefficients, nuclear alpha decay, scanning tunneling microscopy, and qubit superposition.
syllabus.notes: Particles have a non-zero probability of penetrating a barrier higher than their kinetic energy. Qubits exist in linear superposition |psi> = alpha|0> + beta|1>.

courses.title: Cybersecurity & Ethical Hacking Essentials

instructor.name: Alex Vance
instructor.title: Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH) & Red Team Lead

courses.description: Learn defensive cybersecurity, network scanning, OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, cryptography basics, and penetration testing.

syllabus.title: Network Protocols & Port Scanning (Nmap)
syllabus.summary: TCP 3-way handshake, OSI 7-layer model, Wireshark packet capture, and reconnaissance.
syllabus.notes: TCP handshake: SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK. Port 80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS), 22 (SSH), 53 (DNS). Use Nmap for host discovery and service versioning.

syllabus.title: Web Application Security & OWASP Top 10
syllabus.summary: SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), CSRF, Broken Object Level Authorization, and defense strategies.
syllabus.notes: Always use parameterized prepared statements to prevent SQLi. Sanitize and encode user input to eliminate XSS.

syllabus.title: Modern Cryptography: RSA, AES & Hashing
syllabus.summary: Symmetric vs Asymmetric encryption, Public-Key infrastructure, TLS certificates, and salted password hashing (Bcrypt).
syllabus.notes: AES-256 is the gold standard for symmetric encryption. RSA uses large prime factorization for key exchange. Never store plain text passwords; use Argon2 or Bcrypt.

syllabus.title: Defensive Hardening & Incident Response
syllabus.summary: Firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (Snort), Zero Trust architecture, and incident handling protocols.
syllabus.notes: Defense-in-depth ensures that multiple layers of security controls protect crucial assets. Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP) limits account access.

courses.title: Data Structures & Algorithms in Java & C++
courses.description: Conquer coding interviews with mastery over Arrays, Trees, Graphs, Dynamic Programming, Big-O analysis, and recursion patterns.

syllabus.title: Asymptotic Analysis & Big-O Notation
syllabus.summary: Time and Space complexity, Best/Average/Worst case analysis, amortized time.
syllabus.notes: O(1) constant < O(log n) logarithmic < O(n) linear < O(n log n) linearithmic < O(n^2) quadratic < O(2^n) exponential.

syllabus.title: Binary Trees, BSTs & AVL Self-Balancing Trees
syllabus.summary: Tree traversals (Inorder, Preorder, Postorder, Level-Order), insertion, deletion, and rotation logic.
syllabus.notes: In a BST, left child < root < right child. Inorder traversal of a BST yields elements in sorted ascending order. AVL trees maintain balance factor within {-1, 0, 1}.

syllabus.title: Graph Traversal: BFS, DFS & Dijkstra's Algorithm
syllabus.summary: Adjacency lists, Queue-based BFS, Recursive DFS, Cycle detection, and shortest path in weighted graphs.
syllabus.notes: BFS finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs using a Queue. Dijkstra's algorithm utilizes a Priority Queue (Min-Heap) with time complexity O((V + E) log V).

syllabus.title: Dynamic Programming: Memoization & Tabulation
syllabus.summary: Overlapping subproblems, optimal substructure, 0/1 Knapsack, Longest Common Subsequence, and Coin Change.
syllabus.notes: Memoization is top-down caching. Tabulation is bottom-up table filling. Break problems down to base cases and transition relations.

materials.title: Complete Python Programming Comprehensive Revision Notes
materials.subject: Computer Science
materials.description: Condensed cheat-sheet and revision handbook covering syntax, OOP, generators, decorators, exception handling, and standard libraries.
materials.content:
=== SMART EDUCATION SYSTEM: PYTHON STUDY GUIDE ===

1. VARIABLES & DATA TYPES
- Python is dynamically typed. Common types: int, float, str, bool, list, tuple, dict, set.
- Mutable objects can be modified in place (lists, dicts, sets).
- Immutable objects cannot be changed (int, float, str, tuple, frozenset).

2. CONTROL STRUCTURES
- if, elif, else logic blocks.
- for loop iterates over iterables: for item in collection: ...
- while loop executes while condition is true.
- break terminates loop; continue skips current iteration.

3. FUNCTIONS & SCOPE
- Defined using def name(*args, **kwargs):
- Lambda functions: square = lambda x: x ** 2
- LEGB Rule: Local -> Enclosing -> Global -> Built-in.

4. OBJECT-ORIENTED PROGRAMMING (OOP)
- Class definition: class Animal:
- __init__ constructor initializes instance state.
- Inheritance, Encapsulation, Polymorphism, Abstraction.

5. ERROR HANDLING
try:
    result = 10 / divisor
except ZeroDivisionError as err:
    print(f'Error: {err}')
finally:
    cleanup()

6. MEMORY & PERFORMANCE TIPS
- Use generators (yield) for streaming large datasets.
- List comprehensions are faster than manual loops.

materials.title: Calculus & Linear Algebra Formula Sheet & Solved Examples
materials.subject: Mathematics
materials.description: Essential calculus derivatives, integrals, trigonometric identities, matrix transformations, and eigenvalues formula handbook.
materials.content:
=== SMART EDUCATION SYSTEM: CALCULUS & LINEAR ALGEBRA HANDBOOK ===

1. ESSENTIAL DERIVATIVE RULES
- d/dx [x^n] = n * x^(n-1)
- d/dx [sin(x)] = cos(x)
- d/dx [cos(x)] = -sin(x)
- d/dx [e^x] = e^x
- d/dx [ln(x)] = 1/x
- Product Rule: (uv)' = u'v + uv'
- Quotient Rule: (u/v)' = (u'v - uv') / v^2
- Chain Rule: d/dx [f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x)

2. COMMON INTEGRALS
- integral(x^n dx) = (x^(n+1))/(n+1) + C (for n != -1)
- integral(1/x dx) = ln|x| + C
- integral(e^x dx) = e^x + C
- integral(cos(x) dx) = sin(x) + C
- integral(sin(x) dx) = -cos(x) + C
- Integration by parts: integral(u dv) = uv - integral(v du)

3. LINEAR ALGEBRA MATRIX ESSENTIALS
- Determinant of 2x2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] = ad - bc.
- Characteristic equation for Eigenvalues: det(A - lambda*I) = 0.
- Rank of matrix is the maximum number of linearly independent row/column vectors.

materials.content:
=== PREVIOUS YEAR QUESTION PAPER 2023 ===
Subject: General Physics & Electromagnetism
Total Marks: 100 | Time: 3 Hours

KEY HIGHLIGHTS & ANSWER SCHEME:
Q1. State Gauss's Law in electrostatics and derive electric field due to infinite line charge.
Model Solution: The net electric flux through any closed Gaussian surface equals total enclosed charge divided by epsilon_0.
Flux = Integral(E . dA) = Q_enclosed / epsilon_0.
For an infinite line of linear charge density lambda at distance r:
E = lambda / (2 * pi * epsilon_0 * r).

Q2. Explain Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction and Lenz's Law.
EMF = - d(Phi_B) / dt. The negative sign denotes Lenz's law: induced current flows in a direction opposing the magnetic flux change producing it.

materials.title: Top 50 Most Important Web Technologies Q&A (Interview & Exam)
materials.subject: Computer Science
materials.description: Curated list of high-probability questions with expert verified answers, code snippets, and common pitfalls.
materials.content:
=== TOP 50 IMPORTANT WEB TECHNOLOGIES Q&A ===

Q1: What is the Event Loop in JavaScript?
A: The event loop is a runtime mechanism that coordinates asynchronous task queues (Microtask Queue for Promises, Macrotask Queue for setTimeout/setInterval) with the Call Stack. It ensures non-blocking I/O execution on a single main thread.

Q2: What is the difference between CSS Grid and Flexbox?
A: Flexbox is designed for one-dimensional layouts (either a row OR a column), ideal for navbars and linear element sequences. CSS Grid is designed for two-dimensional layouts (rows AND columns simultaneously), ideal for complete page templates.

Q3: What are HTTP Status Codes 200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, and 500?
A: 200: OK, 201: Created, 400: Bad Request (malformed input), 401: Unauthorized (missing auth), 403: Forbidden (authenticated but lack permission), 404: Not Found, 500: Internal Server Error.

materials.title: Machine Learning & Neural Networks Quick Revision Handbook
materials.subject: Artificial Intelligence
materials.description: Supervised, unsupervised algorithms, backpropagation math, activation functions (ReLU, Sigmoid, Softmax), and loss functions.
materials.content:
=== MACHINE LEARNING CONCISE CHEATSHEET ===

1. LOSS FUNCTIONS
- Mean Squared Error (MSE) for regression: 1/N * sum((y - y_hat)^2)
- Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) for binary classification: -[y*log(p) + (1-y)*log(1-p)]
- Categorical Cross-Entropy for multi-class classification.

2. ACTIVATION FUNCTIONS
- Sigmoid: f(x) = 1 / (1 + e^-x), outputs (0, 1). Susceptible to vanishing gradient.
- ReLU: f(x) = max(0, x), avoids vanishing gradients for positive inputs.
- Softmax: Normalizes logits into a probability distribution summing to 1.0.

3. REGULARIZATION TECHNIQUES
- L1 (Lasso): Adds absolute weights penalty lambda*sum(|w|). Promotes sparsity.
- L2 (Ridge): Adds squared weights penalty lambda*sum(w^2). Prevents large weights.
- Dropout: Randomly disables neurons during training with probability p to prevent co-adaptation.

exams.title: Python Programming & Algorithms Mastery
exams.description: Test your mastery over Python data structures, algorithms, syntax nuance, and object-oriented principles.

questions.question: What is the output of `bool([])` and `bool([0])` in Python?
questions.explanation: An empty list `[]` evaluates to falsy (`False`), whereas a non-empty list `[0]` has length 1 and evaluates to truthy (`True`).

questions.question: What is the average time complexity of searching for an element in a Python dictionary?
questions.explanation: Python dictionaries are implemented as hash tables, providing average O(1) time complexity for key lookups.

questions.question: Which of the following data structures is immutable in Python?
questions.explanation: Tuples cannot be altered after creation, making them immutable and hashable if their elements are also immutable.

questions.question: What keyword is used to create a generator function in Python?
questions.explanation: The `yield` keyword pauses function execution and returns a generator iterator value, retaining local variable state.

questions.question: What will `[x * 2 for x in range(5) if x % 2 == 0]` evaluate to?
questions.explanation: The even values in range(5) are 0, 2, 4. Multiplying each by 2 yields [0, 4, 8].

questions.question: Which method is called automatically when an instance of a Python class is instantiated?
questions.explanation: `__init__` is the constructor method used to initialize an instance's state.

questions.question: What does the `*args` syntax in a function definition indicate?
options: Variable number of positional arguments as a tuple
questions.explanation: `*args` allows passing any number of positional arguments, collected as a tuple.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `with` statement in Python?
options: Looping through a file line by line
Automatic context management and resource release
questions.explanation: `with` invokes the context manager protocol (`__enter__` and `__exit__`), guaranteeing resource cleanup like closing files.

questions.question: What is the output of `type(lambda x: x)`?
questions.explanation: Lambdas in Python are first-class instances of `<class 'function'>`.

questions.question: Which built-in module is used to measure execution time of small code snippets in Python?
questions.explanation: `timeit` is specifically designed for accurately benchmarking short Python statements by disabling garbage collection spikes.

exams.title: Calculus & Linear Algebra Final Test
exams.description: Assess your skills in differential calculus, definite integrals, and matrix transformations.

questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = ln(3x^2)?
questions.explanation: Using chain rule or log rules: ln(3x^2) = ln(3) + 2*ln(x). Derivative of ln(3) is 0; derivative of 2*ln(x) is 2/x.

questions.question: Evaluate integral from 0 to 1 of (3x^2 + 2x) dx:
questions.explanation: Antiderivative is x^3 + x^2. Evaluated from 0 to 1: (1^3 + 1^2) - 0 = 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.question: What is the determinant of matrix [[4, 2], [3, 5]]?
If matrix A is invertible, what is det(A^-1)?
questions.explanation: Since det(A * A^-1) = det(I) = 1, it follows that det(A^-1) = 1 / det(A).

questions.question: What is the limit of (sin x) / x as x approaches 0?
questions.explanation: This fundamental trigonometric limit evaluates to 1, as proven by the Squeeze Theorem or L'Hopital's Rule.

questions.question: What represents the direction of steepest ascent for a multivariable function f(x, y)?
questions.explanation: The gradient vector grad(f) points in the exact direction of greatest rate of increase of the function.

questions.question: What is the integral of e^(2x) dx?
questions.explanation: By substitution u = 2x, du = 2 dx, the integral becomes (1/2) * e^(2x) + C.

questions.question: Two vectors u and v are orthogonal if and only if their dot product u . v is equal to:
questions.explanation: u . v = |u||v| cos(90 deg) = 0.

questions.question: What are the eigenvalues of identity matrix I of size 3x3?
questions.explanation: Since I*v = 1*v for any non-zero vector, all eigenvalues of the identity matrix are 1.

questions.question: What is the second derivative of f(x) = sin(x)?
questions.explanation: First derivative is cos(x). Derivative of cos(x) is -sin(x).

exams.title: Modern Web Development Fundamentals
exams.description: Evaluate understanding of modern HTML5, CSS Flexbox & Grid, JavaScript Promises, and REST architecture.

questions.question: Which HTML5 tag is the most semantic choice for self-contained blog posts or news items?
questions.explanation: `<article>` represents a self-contained composition in a document intended to be independently distributable or reusable.

questions.question: In CSS Flexbox, which property aligns items along the cross axis?
questions.explanation: `justify-content` aligns items along the main axis, while `align-items` aligns along the cross axis.

questions.question: Which JavaScript method turns a JSON string into a JavaScript object?
questions.explanation: `JSON.parse()` deserializes a JSON string into an object, while `JSON.stringify()` serializes an object into a JSON string.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between `localStorage` and `sessionStorage`?
options: localStorage only stores strings, sessionStorage stores objects
localStorage data persists when browser is closed, sessionStorage expires when the tab is closed
localStorage is limited to 1KB, sessionStorage is 5MB
localStorage cannot be accessed by JavaScript
questions.explanation: localStorage data has no expiration date, while sessionStorage is cleared whenever the page session ends (tab closed).

questions.question: Which HTTP status code signifies that a resource was successfully created on the server?
questions.explanation: 201 Created indicates that the request succeeded and resulted in the creation of a new resource.

questions.question: What does the `async` keyword placed before a function declaration do?
options: Runs the function in a background Web Worker thread
Forces the function to always return a Promise
Makes all variables in the function immutable
Prevents other functions from running concurrently
questions.explanation: `async` functions automatically wrap return values in a resolved Promise and permit using `await` inside.

questions.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the font-size of the root element (<html>)?
questions.explanation: `rem` stands for 'root em', which is calculated relative to the root element's font size (typically 16px by default).

questions.question: What is the purpose of CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)?
options: To encrypt network packets using TLS
To allow or restrict resources requested on a web page from another domain outside the domain from which the first resource was served
To compress HTTP responses with Gzip
questions.explanation: CORS is an HTTP-header based security mechanism enabling servers to specify which origins are permitted to access their assets.

questions.question: What does the JavaScript spread operator `...` do when applied to an array?
options: Expands array elements into individual arguments or elements
Sorts the array in ascending order
questions.explanation: The spread operator `...` expands an iterable into individual elements, commonly used for shallow copying and concatenating arrays.

questions.question: Which array method creates a new array with all elements that pass the test implemented by the provided function?
questions.explanation: `filter()` iterates through each item and includes it in a new array only if the callback returns truthy.
